text: Git branching is a powerful feature of version control that helps teams work on different parts of a project simultaneously. Typically, developers create feature branches to build new features or fix bugs without affecting the main codebase. For example, you might create a branch called "add-login-page" to work on user authentication. Once the work is complete, you merge that branch back into the main branch. In many workflows, this is done through a pull request, which allows others to review the code before it is added. This structured version control workflow keeps the project stable and helps teams collaborate more efficiently.
